name: Multiclass Hate Speech Detection
description: The model is adept at identifying various forms of hate speech in textual content, particularly targeting tweets. It leverages the RoBERTa base model architecture and is trained on a diversified dataset to discern multiple categories of hate speech including sexism, racism, religious bigotry, and more. The model is capable of distinguishing between seven different classes of hateful language, providing a nuanced understanding that goes beyond a binary hate or not-hate classification. It's an invaluable asset in moderating online discussions, ensuring a respectful and inclusive communication environment. By utilizing this model, platforms can automate the process of flagging and managing hateful content, promoting a healthier online discourse.
examples: Detecting gender-based hate speech in online articles
Analyzing hate speech trends on social media platforms
Identifying hate speech in political discourse
Monitoring hate speech in online gaming communities
Detecting hate speech in movie reviews
Analyzing hate speech in celebrity tweets
Monitoring hate speech in news comment sections

name: Binary Hate Speech Detection

The model's binary classification approach allows for a clear-cut decision, aiding in the moderation of online discussions and social media posts.
